title: Alcohol use reduces efficacy of immunotherapy by disrupting antitumor immunity

comments.content: This could be an interesting finding for human health. Its also terrible that we learn this by getting mice drunk and watching how their cancer outlook compares to sober mice.
In mice. Moderate to heavy alcohol intake (not sure how it converts to human dose)

But alcohol intake is associated with elevated cancer risk[1], so this would be more about the mechanism, no?

Or does those mechanisms vary substantially between mice and men, so to speak?

[1]: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10867516/

Allegedly (AI summary) 2.5g/kg/day or ~3 drinks/day for "moderate" and 5g/kg/day or ~6 drinks/day for "heavy." But mg/kg is never a perfect translation, just a rough approximation, so keep that in mind as well.
Does this specific batch of rodents convert alcohol to acetaldehyde at the same rate as humans? Do they clear it out at the same rate? Does the poison have as deleterious effects on other systems?
In related news, poison not good for health
Maybe not, but please don't post unsubstantive comments to Hacker News.
Note that the impact observed here was for mice on some mouse-specific experimental immunotherapy drug. The drunk mice not on the immunotherapy drug were not negatively impacted.
The dose makes the poison, and measuring it is important.

isn't the latest on alcohol that no amount of it is harmless, like with lead?

and not in the "technically nothing is ever just one way or another" way but in like a properly substantive way?

Some people could have a 80% greater risk of cancer and others 3%, or whatever the actual numbers are; just making the general point.

Margin of error is a thing meaning some people could call outside the analysis altogether

Media also shape belief/behavior through frequency of reporting:

https://ourworldindata.org/does-the-news-reflect-what-we-die...

Normalizing along stats is riddled with bias as no one knows it all/sees it all

That said I quit drinking in 2019 cold turkey just cuz...I dunno. Just seemed like I was over that phase of life :shrug emoji:
